about: The Haftarah from the Prophets (Malachi 1:1–2:7) opens with “I have loved Jacob, but Esau I have hated,” God’s answer to the twins born in this portion. It goes on to call the priests back to the true instruction (Torah) that should be in their mouths. The reading from the Apostles (Romans 9:1–18) quotes the same verse from Malachi. Shaul grieves for his own people, “to whom belong the adoption, the glory, the covenants,” and shows that God’s election rests on his mercy, not on human merit.
